Honestly? That's the best solution that can reasonably be expected, given the limitations of the hardware. For a first person shooter, I think 60 fps is worth sacrificing visual fidelity. Hell, even in stuff like Assassin's Creed, I would have preferred dynamic resolution to the ridiculously aggressive LOD pop-in that we got in Unity.

Now, of course it would be preferable for the art team to rein in their vision to match the capabilities of the engine, but if it's a matter of not being able to render frames fast enough only in certain situations, I think the dynamic resolution technique is probably the way to go.

Doesn't change the fact that I'm not touching this game until I can play it on more powerful PC hardware. Given Warzone's MOBA qualities, I'm almost positive it will end up seeing a PC release.
